Subject: QuantifAI RFP: Dedicated Reservation & GPU Slotting Details

Hi Mateo,

Thanks for taking this RFP — we are evaluating dedicated reservation options for a new realtime inference product. Attached is our RFP form (QuantifAI_RFP_form_v2.pdf) with the high-level requirements. We want a detailed workbook that maps:
- Recommended GPU families for a mixed workload (conversational + embeddings + short reranking tasks)
- Expected token throughput and guidance per GPU family (A100, H100, L4-class) for 512-token average prompts and p99 tail latency targets
- Reservation sizing for predictable monthly committed capacity vs burst lanes (we expect 2x seasonal peak in Q1)
- Cost delta if we prefer lower latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and preemption rules

Key context:
- Peak concurrent streams: target is ~600 concurrent conversational streams at 512 tokens average, but usage is spiky (90th-99th percentile differs by factor ~3).
- SLOs: 95ms p95 and 200ms p99 for the primary conversational model; embeddings can tolerate higher latency.
- Mixed model mix: conversational 55%, embeddings 30%, reranking 15% (by request count).

Can you return a draft workbook with numeric assumptions (tokens/sec, batch sizes, expected QPS per GPU), a recommended reserved pool (by node count + GPU type) and an explanation of how Redwood handles burst lanes and automatic fallback? Also flag any gaps where we need telemetry (e.g., per-route token distribution).

We'd like this back before our procurement window closes on 2026-11-08.

Thanks,
Lisa Turner
Head of Platform Partnerships
QuantifAI

Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the RFP form. We attached a first-pass workbook (20261101-quantifai-reserve-workbook.xlsx) and a brief MAAP (minimum acceptable architecture plan) PDF that outlines our sizing methodology and assumptions (redwood-reservation-maap-draft.pdf). High-level summary below; the workbook contains the numeric cells and sensitivity tabs.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Baseline reserve: 16 x H100 (80GB) nodes as the committed pool. Rationale: best fit for conversational model with 512-token average to meet 200ms p99 at 600 concurrent streams assuming adaptive batching and low-quantization FP16/4-bit mix.
- Burst lanes: additional shared burst capacity composed of 8 x A100 80GB on-demand and automatic routing to smaller L4-like instances for embeddings and reranking when cost-constrained.
- Throughput assumptions included in workbook: per-H100 sustained concurrent streams (512 tokens avg, dynamic batching) = ~45-55 concurrent streams per GPU card at p95 95ms; p99 headroom reduces concurrent to ~32 streams/card.
- Autoscaling policy: target to maintain p95 < 95ms; autoscale on queue length and observed token/sec. We recommend a burst reservation (non-committed) equivalent to ~50% of peak committed capacity to handle 2x spikes.
- Fallbacks: model variant pinning and automatic downgrade to a smaller quantized variant with graceful quality degradation; routing policy to send low-priority rerank/emb requests to lower-cost nodes.

Gaps we flagged for you to confirm (included as comments in the workbook):
1) Exact prompt/token distribution per route (we used your 512 average but need the full distribution).
2) Acceptable cost vs latency tradeoffs for reranking (do you want strict latency for rerank?).
3) Preemption tolerance for background jobs (embeddings pipelining preemptible?).

Next steps: if this mapping looks good we'll convert the workbook into a formal reserved commitment proposal (with per-node pricing, commit term options 12/24/36 months) and a deployment runbook. Can we schedule 30 minutes for Tuesday 2026-11-03 10:00-11:00 PT to walk the workbook?

Best,
Mateo Alvarez

Thanks — quick clarifications before the call:
- Our conversational model has a bimodal prompt distribution: 70% short (<=128 tokens), 30% long (>=1024 tokens). The 512 average you used is fine as long as the workbook shows sensitivity for the two modes.
- Embeddings jobs are often batched (bulk embed jobs overnight) but also have a small realtime path (single-item). You mentioned routing embeddings to L4-class nodes — what's the expected per-card throughput for L4 when handling both bulk and single-item paths?
- For p99 calculation, do your numbers assume warm KV cache for streaming contexts, or cold starts? We need clarity because upstream will demand p99 on cold starts for SLA negotiations.

See you on the call — we've penciled in 2026-11-03 10:00 PT.

—Lisa

Hi Lisa / QuantifAI team —

Great call earlier. Per our discussion, here are the concrete technical assumptions we populated into the workbook and how they map to your SLAs. I’m pasting the abbreviated technical sheet here; full formulas are in the workbook.

Assumptions and per-GPU guidance:
- H100 (80GB, top-end):
  • Target mix: conversational heavy (intended primary pool).
  • Dynamic batching behavior (512 token avg): typical batch size 6-12 depending on simultaneity.
  • Sustained p95 throughput per GPU card: ~50 concurrent streams (512 avg) -> ~100k tokens/sec/card.
  • Sustained p99 throughput per GPU card: ~32 concurrent streams -> ~65k tokens/sec/card.
  • Cold-start latency multiplier: +25-60ms depending on model size and KV warm state. We assume warm KV for p95 numbers; p99 cold-start provisioning is handled via reserved underlying capacity and burst lanes.

- A100 (80GB):
  • Good cost-performance for quantized variants and mid-term bursts.
  • p95 throughput per card: ~40 concurrent streams (512 avg). p99: ~26 streams.

- L4-class (24–48GB inference-optimized):
  • Best for embeddings and short-text reranking in cost-sensitive paths.
  • Single-item embed latency: ~12–35ms depending on model; bulk embed throughput scales with batch size (we assume batching to 128 items yields ~1500–3000 embeds/sec per card).

Reservation sizing example (from workbook, rounded):
- Baseline committed pool: 16 x H100 nodes -> supports ~512 concurrent conversational streams at p95 and p99 headroom as described. This assumes a 5% reserved room for leader election and health drains.
- Burst on-demand lane: 8 x A100 nodes available for 2x seasonal spikes; automatic routing policy will shift lower-priority rerank/emb requests first.
- Cost-optimized lane: L4-class fleet serving embeddings and rerank with routing thresholds to avoid impacting conversational SLOs.

Operational controls we recommend:
- Canary and staged rollout: start with 20% traffic on reserved pool, measure live p99; expand in 20% increments.
- Analytics required: per-route token histograms, per-node token/sec, queue length percentiles, and p99 time-series.
- Fallback rules: if p99 exceeds threshold for >5 minutes, automatically divert new sessions to a lower-latency model variant until scaled.

Deliverables we will provide in the finalized proposal: committed pricing table (12/24/36 mo), formal SLA clause language for p95/p99, runbook for onboarding (network/VPC peering, KMS integration), and a migration checklist for model pinning and traffic routing.

If you confirm the bimodal token split and cold-start requirement for p99 we will iterate the workbook sensitivity tabs and produce an updated committed proposal (price + node mix + term options).

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
